timeline.message:
Protect NodeConnectionsService from stale conns

A call to `ConnectionTarget#connect` which happens strictly after all
calls that close connections should leave us connected to the target.
However concurrent calls to `ConnectionTarget#connect` can overlap, and
today this means that a connection returned from an earlier call may
overwrite one from a later call. The trouble is that the earlier
connection attempt may yield a closed connection (it was concurrent with
the disconnections) so we must not let it supersede the newer one.

With this commit we impose a linear order on the connection attempts,
and avoid earlier attempts from overwriting the connections resulting
from later attempts.

When combined with #92546, closes #92029
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body: I love this ASCII workflow art :100:
Would it make sense to reset seqNoGenerator to 0 as well?
Could theoretically overflow, but I guess it's a very remote corner case.

Also nice find! LGTM but I wonder if using a lock instead of atomic references would make all this ConnectionTarget's implementation much easier? I am not sure the effort justifies any potential performance benefits, as I imagine it is not expected to have high concurrency on opening/closing connections to a specific node.
Yeah on reflection I don't like this as much as the other idea, closing this.
